in_hebrew.name: אליזבטה
in_hebrew.meaning: אלוהים הוא השופט שלי, אלוהים הוא שבועתי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: אליזבטה היא השם העברי הנגזר מהשם אלישבע, שפירושו 'אלוהים הוא השופט שלי' או 'אלוהים הוא שבועתי'. השם אלישבע מורכב משתי מילים עבריות: אל וישבע, שפירושם אלוהים ושבועה, בהתאמה. השם אליזבטה הוא גרסה נוצרית של השם העברי אלישבע, והוא משמש כמחווה לאליזבט, אם יוחנן המטביל, בברית החדשה.

in_greek.name: Ελισάβεττα
in_greek.meaning: Ο Θεός είναι η δικαιοσύνη μου, Ο Θεός είναι ο όρκος μου
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Ελισάβεττα είναι η ελληνική εκδοχή του εβραϊκού ονόματος אלישבע (אלישבע), που σημαίνει 'Ο Θεός είναι η δικαιοσύνη μου' ή 'Ο Θεός είναι ο όρκος μου'. Το όνομα προέρχεται από τις εβραϊκές λέξεις אל (אל) που σημαίνει Θεός και ישבע (ישבע) που σημαίνει δικαιοσύνη ή όρκος. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, η Ελισάβετ είναι η μητέρα του Ιωάννη του Βαπτιστή.

in_latin.name: Elisabetta
in_latin.meaning: Deus est iustitia mea, Deus est iuramentum meum
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Elisabetta derivatur ex nomine hebraico אלישבע (Elisheva), quod significat 'Deus est iustitia mea' vel 'Deus est iuramentum meum'. Nomen constat ex duabus vocibus hebraicis: אל (El) quod est Deus et ישבע (yishbeva) quod est iustitia vel iuramentum. In Ecclesia Christiana, Elisabetta est forma Latina nominis Elisabeth, matris Ioannis Baptistae.

in_english.name: Elisabetta
in_english.meaning: God is my justice, God is my oath
in_english.long_meaning: The name Elisabetta is of Hebrew origin, derived from the name Elisheva (אלישבע), meaning 'God is my justice' or 'God is my oath'. It consists of two Hebrew words: El (אל) meaning God and yishbeva (ישבע) meaning justice or oath. In Christian tradition, Elisabetta is associated with Elizabeth, the mother of John the Baptist in the New Testament. The name symbolizes faith, devotion, and divine promise.

data.cultural_impact: The name Elisabetta has been popular throughout history, particularly in the Christian world. Elisabetta was a common name among the Italian nobility during the Renaissance period. It also gained popularity during the Baroque period in Europe. The name is derived from the Hebrew name Elisheba, which has its roots in the Old Testament, specifically in the story of Elisabeth, the mother of John the Baptist. Thus, the name carries a rich historical and cultural significance, evoking images of royalty, spiritual devotion, and biblical importance.
data.spiritual_significance: In the biblical account, Elisabeth was a barren woman, and her Child John the Baptist was to prepare the way for Jesus, the Messiah. The name Elisabetta, therefore, carries a spiritual significance rooted in faith, hope, and the memory of God's promises. Elisabeth's faithfulness and perseverance inspire those who bear her name to trust in God's plan and hold steadfast in their beliefs. Like Elisabeth, we can turn to God in our moments of doubt and remember His promises, no matter our circumstances. Elisabeth's name is a reminder of the miracle-working power of God, who can bring even the most barren of hearts to life.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Elisabetta, derived from the Hebrew name Elisheba, means "God is my oath" or "God is my promise." It is a name rich in devotion and faith, reminding us of God's covenants and promises to His people.
